title: Regulatory subunit NEMO promotes polyubiquitin-dependent induction of NF-kappaB through a targetable second interaction with upstream activator IKK2.
authors: Ko, Myung Soo; Cohen, Samantha N; Polley, Smarajit; Mahata, Sushil K; Biswas, Tapan; Huxford, Tom; Ghosh, Gourisankar
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NEMO与IKK2蛋白间的泛素依赖性互作及NF-kappaB信号调控，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Canonical NF-kappaB signaling through the inhibitor of kappaB kinase (IKK) complex requires induction of IKK2/IKKbeta subunit catalytic activity via specific phosphorylation within its activation loop. This process is known to be dependent upon the accessory ubiquitin (Ub)-binding subunit NF-kappaB essential modulator (NEMO)/IKKgamma as well as poly-Ub chains. However, the mechanism through which poly-Ub binding serves to promote IKK catalytic activity is unclear. Here, we show that binding of NEMO/IKKgamma to linear poly-Ub promotes a second interaction between NEMO/IKKgamma and IKK2/IKKbeta, distinct from the well-characterized interaction of the NEMO/IKKgamma N terminus to the "NEMO-binding domain" at the C terminus of IKK2/IKKbeta. We mapped the location of this second interaction to a stretch of roughly six amino acids immediately N-terminal to the zinc finger domain in human NEMO/IKKgamma. We also showed that amino acid residues within this region of NEMO/IKKgamma are necessary for binding to IKK2/IKKbeta through this secondary interaction in vitro and for full activation of IKK2/IKKbeta in cultured cells. Furthermore, we identified a docking site for this segment of NEMO/IKKgamma on IKK2/IKKbeta within its scaffold-dimerization domain proximal to the kinase domain-Ub-like domain. Finally, we showed that a peptide derived from this region of NEMO/IKKgamma is capable of interfering specifically with canonical NF-kappaB signaling in transfected cells. These in vitro biochemical and cell culture-based experiments suggest that, as a consequence of its association with linear poly-Ub, NEMO/IKKgamma plays a direct role in priming IKK2/IKKbeta for phosphorylation and that this process can be inhibited to specifically disrupt canonical NF-kappaB signaling.
abstract_zh: 通过抑制因子κB激酶（IKK）复合物的经典NF-κB信号传导，需要在其激活环内通过特异性磷酸化诱导IKK2/IKKbeta亚基催化活性。已知此过程依赖于辅助性泛素（Ub）结合亚基NF-κB必需调节因子（NEMO）/IKKgamma以及多聚Ub链。然而，多聚Ub结合促进IKK催化活性的机制尚不清楚。在此，我们表明NEMO/IKKgamma与线性多聚Ub的结合促进了NEMO/IKKgamma与IKK2/IKKbeta之间的第二次相互作用，这不同于已充分表征的NEMO/IKKgamma N端与IKK2/IKKbeta C端“NEMO结合域”的相互作用。我们将此第二次相互作用的位置定位在人类NEMO/IKKgamma中锌指结构域紧邻N端的一段约六个氨基酸序列上。我们还证明，NEMO/IKKgamma此区域内的氨基酸残基对于在体外通过这种次级相互作用与IKK2/IKKbeta结合以及在培养细胞中完全激活IKK2/IKKbeta是必需的。此外，我们在IKK2/IKKbeta的支架-二聚化结构域内，靠近激酶结构域-泛素样结构域处，鉴定了NEMO/IKKgamma此片段的对接位点。最后，我们表明源自NEMO/IKKgamma此区域的一个肽段能够在转染细胞中特异性地干扰经典NF-κB信号传导。这些体外生化和细胞培养实验表明，作为其与线性多聚Ub结合的结果，NEMO/IKKgamma在启动IKK2/IKKbeta磷酸化中发挥直接作用，并且此过程可被抑制以特异性破坏经典NF-κB信号传导。
